claim: The colour a shadow shifts toward, chosen by a colour designer and worth roughly half a film's identity. Blue shift is the modern default and reads clean; warm shift reads nostalgic; grey multiply reads cheap and flat.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: shadows in a darker shade of the base color, monochromatic shading
complementary color shadows, contrasting hue shading

review.issue: darker_same_hue's clause "shadows in a darker shade of the base color, monochromatic shading" is a sentence, not tags, and "monochromatic" risks pulling the whole frame toward greyscale - the opposite of what the option means. complementary ("complementary color shadows, contrasting hue shading") is not a tag either and against this subject (dark red hair, black jersey) will most likely just produce the same cool shadows as blue_shift.
review.fix: darker_same_hue -> empty clause and declare it the baseline (darker-same-hue is what the model does by default). complementary -> name the actual hue the subject implies, e.g. "green shadows, teal toned shading", or drop it.
